A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BridgeDrive research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated, and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Bench2Drive simulations, including BridgeDrive's 72.27% success rate, model and waypoint ablations, inference timings, and driving case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original Bench2Drive results and adds NAVSIM evaluation and experiments on anchor selection, diffusion refinement, and anchor count.

M1.justification: The proposed anchor construction, classifier, diffusion-bridge denoiser, training objectives, and ODE planning procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3. The added regression and classification models are experimental controls, while varying anchor count changes configurations rather than the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates BridgeDrive on Bench2Drive and mentions NAVSIM only as background. v2 adds actual NAVSIM navtest evaluation in Appendix B.4 and Table 6, extending coverage beyond reactive CARLA closed-loop driving to a distinct nonreactive planning benchmark.

E2.justification: v2 adds anchor classification without diffusion refinement and anchor-based regression as substantive controls in Table 9. The new NAVSIM comparison includes VADv2, Hydra-MDP, and published and reproduced DiffusionDrive results. DiffusionDrivegeo also joins Table 1's comparator set, although its evaluation already appeared in v1's Table 2.

E3.justification: v2 adds NAVSIM navtest evaluation with PDMS and its component metrics, tests selecting second- through fourth-ranked anchors, and sweeps anchor counts, including up to 1,000 for anchor classification. Previously stated Bench2Drive route and training settings remain. The revised headline scores match the 60-anchor entry in Table 9, but Appendix C.3 still specifies 20 anchors, leaving the main-result configuration incompletely reconciled.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests sensitivity to anchor-selection rank, a single-anchor configuration, removal of diffusion refinement, regression without time embedding, and anchor count. These directly examine the contributions of anchor priors, classification, and refinement beyond v1's diffusion-model and waypoint comparisons. The existing driving case studies, including the out-of-distribution failure, are retained.

E5.justification: Table 6 newly distinguishes DiffusionDrive's published result from a reproduction using a different seed. Both versions already state three-seed evaluation for models exceeding prior SOTA and report uncertainty with ± values in Table 2. No explicit increase in repetitions for retained experiments or new statistical testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces BridgeDrive's DS/SR of 86.87/72.27% with 87.99/74.99%, alongside updates in Tables 2–4. These are revised reports, not an established same-setting gain, given the anchor-count ambiguity. New results include NAVSIM PDMS 88.0 versus DiffusionDrive's published 88.1 and reproduced 87.6, declining performance with lower-ranked anchors, and peak BridgeDrive success at 60 anchors. Table 4 corrects the overtaking comparison to a 4.44-point deficit against ORION, although its caption remains inconsistent. Section 4.3 newly reports a 4.09-point full-diffusion waypoint gain, while unchanged Table 2 values imply 9.09.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, diffusion-bridge SDE and probability-flow ODE, score approximation, and loss equations remain unchanged. The expanded appendices add empirical evidence and discussion, without new theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion strengthen the quantitative Bench2Drive claim from a 5-point to a 7.72-point success-rate advantage. The central contributions—principled anchor-guided diffusion bridges, symmetric forward/reverse processes, and compatibility with efficient ODE planning—remain the same.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 newly limits the waypoint-superiority conclusion primarily to Bench2Drive and emphasizes that general superiority remains unresolved. B.2 explains runtime through perception and attention costs, B.4 attributes NAVSIM near-parity to benchmark saturation, and Appendix D interprets anchor resilience, refinement benefits, and the tradeoff between diversity and classification accuracy. Figure 1's caption explicitly identifies catastrophic anchor-selection failure. Existing lidar, comfort, and out-of-distribution limitations remain.

D1.justification: B.2 newly specifies 8×2 or 11×2 trajectory matrices, and D.2 describes constructing the regression control by removing time embedding. Existing data filtering, frozen perception backbone, optimizer, diffusion schedule, and ten-epoch H20 training details are retained. No new code or data access information is provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Learning from All Vehicles, nuPlan, and DriveArena. Appendix B.5 expands discussion of waypoint and control choices in already-cited TransFuser++, SimLingo, and DriveGPT4-V2. The main related-work section and central positioning against truncated diffusion remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are retained, with local grammar, author-contribution marker, caption, and cross-reference edits. Appendix B gains two subsections and a revised heading, and new Appendix D organizes the added ablations. These are localized extensions rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds NAVSIM and anchor-study Tables 6, 8, and 9; v1's architecture Table 6 becomes Table 7. Table 1 gains a comparator row, Table 2 moves below its discussion, and several captions change. Figures 1–7 retain identical artwork, with otherwise local layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the new anchor-only and regression controls provide more direct evidence for diffusion refinement, NAVSIM broadens empirical support, and Appendix B.5 appropriately bounds waypoint conclusions. These gains improve the paper, but their overall benefit is limited by unclear linkage of headline scores to the 60-anchor configuration despite C.3's 20-anchor statement, and the newly incorrect full-diffusion gain in Section 4.3.
